visual_brief: Shanghai Tower is a rounded, tapering glass skyscraper whose façade twists upward into an asymmetric curved crown without a needle spire. Nearby plaza views reveal its spiral, while elevated and Bund-side views establish its scale in Lujiazui. Distinguish it from Jin Mao's tiered silhouette, the World Financial Center's trapezoidal opening and the Oriental Pearl Tower's spheres.
notes: Six verified photographs retained. Preferred: c1 for daylight or c3 for dusk. c1–c4 have 2000 px long sides. Several alternatives have obscured bases; c4 is historical and retains a crane. ArchDaily provides credits without a reuse licence; Gensler states All Rights Reserved. Publication rights are therefore not cleared for every candidate.
